researcher_notes:
Checked all 120 assigned backlog rows (83 unique URLs, since the original 2026-07-21 crawler's fuzzy brand-matching frequently attached the same URL to multiple different brand names). Of the 120 rows, 45 were confirmed as genuine named-customer relationships (write-ups below collapse near-duplicate rows pointing at the same underlying story into a single record with notes flagging the duplication -- see Papa Johns, Torchy's Tacos, Big Chicken, Cracker Barrel, Au Bon Pain, Gong Cha, and Burgerville for examples -- so the records array below has fewer than 45 entries even though 45 rows independently confirmed real relationships). 1 row hit a dead link (404) on partech.com. The remaining 74 rows were rejected as not confirming a real relationship for the assigned brand. 

By far the dominant failure pattern (accounting for the large majority of rejects) was pure brand-name fuzzy-matching noise: the crawler attached a brand name to a URL where that brand is never mentioned anywhere on the page. This was extreme for two brands in particular: 'Pizza Ranch' was matched to 8 different Restaurant365 franchisee case studies (IHOP, Jimmy John's, Whataburger, Taco John's, Carl's Jr., Dave's Hot Chicken, Tropical Smoothie Cafe, Blaze Pizza franchisees) -- none mention Pizza Ranch at all, each is a genuine case study about a completely different brand's franchisee. 'Pizza Press, The' was matched to roughly 30 Crunchtime and PAR press/blog URLs covering unrelated topics (other named restaurant brands' case studies, executive appointments, funding announcements, award-show finalist news, partner-program launches, and even a movie theater chain and gas-station convenience stores) -- 'Pizza Press' does not appear on any of them; this looks like a matching artifact triggered by the word 'press' appearing in Crunchtime's /press/ URL path rather than any real signal about a Pizza Press customer relationship. 'Ward's Restaurant' showed a similar pattern, matched to 8 URLs that turned out to be PAR/R365 customer-awards or loyalty-program announcements (RaceWay, EG America, Punchh awards, R365 Customer Excellence Awards) where 'award(s)' in the URL/title appears to have triggered a fuzzy match to 'Ward's' -- none mention Ward's Restaurant. 'Stand Restaurants, The' and 'Taco Stand, The' were both matched to a generic R365 blog post about satisfaction-metric definitions with no named customers at all, and to the same Crunchtime Pressed-Juicery/Gong-cha article (which does not mention either). 'Country Kitchen', 'California Pizza Kitchen', 'Calif Chicken Cafe', 'Burger Village', and 'Village Inn' [partial] were similarly mismatched onto pages that were genuinely about a different, unrelated brand. 

A second, more subtle failure mode: brand mismatch between similarly-named but distinct companies. 'Black Rock Bar & Grill' was matched to an R365 case study that is genuinely a named customer relationship -- but the actual customer is Black Rock Coffee Bar, a drive-thru coffee chain, not Black Rock Bar & Grill; rejected as the wrong entity despite the page being a real, high-quality case study. 

One dead link: the PAR/NomadGo AI-counting-solution press release (partech.com/press-releases/par-technology-and-nomadgo-partner-...) returned HTTP 404. 

Among the 45 confirmed rows, several resolve to the SAME underlying vendor-brand relationship already captured elsewhere and are flagged explicitly in the record notes to prevent double-counting when Todd merges into the graph: Papa Johns/PAR (duplicates a record already in phase2_pos_evidence_draft_2026-08-03.json), Torchy's Tacos/PAR Punchh (duplicates phase2_loyalty_evidence_draft_2026-08-03.json), and Big Chicken/PAR (two backlog URLs both independently confirm the same relationship already in phase2_pos_evidence_draft_2026-08-03.json). 

Among genuinely new confirmed relationships, a recurring pattern is franchisee-level rather than brand-wide evidence: Taco Bell (via MAS Restaurant Group on PAR, and via BLCO Enterprises on R365), Five Guys (Five Guys NY on R365), Blaze Pizza (Millennial Restaurant Group on R365), Village Inn (Walker Group on R365), and Long John Silver's (Charter Foods on PAR) are all single-franchisee deployments, not confirmed brand-standard/corporate decisions -- scored with vendor_role=franchisee_deployment and deployment_status=franchisee_deployment_not_brand_standard accordingly, per the same conservative convention used in the earlier Phase 2 POS pass. Several other confirmed records are old (2010-2014, even 2011) Crunchtime press releases for brands with known subsequent corporate turmoil (Le Pain Quotidien's 2020 bankruptcy, Fuddruckers' multiple ownership changes, Au Bon Pain's restructuring) -- these are flagged in notes as likely stale and not recommended for graph promotion without independent reconfirmation of current status.
